basics.name: Asen Dotsinski
basics.summary: I'm an AI researcher driven to keep increasingly capable AI safe as it proliferates, focusing on the adversarial robustness of open-weight LLMs against jailbreaking. I'm a PhD student in LLM security at INSAIT and first author of published work on jailbreaking and LLM interpretability.

publications.name: Sockpuppetting: Jailbreaking LLMs by Combining Prefilling with Optimization
publications.publisher: Second Workshop on Agents in the Wild: Safety, Security, and Beyond
publications.summary: A jailbreaking method achieving up to 99% success rate with no optimization, and improving on optimization-based baselines with a hybrid approach by up to 64% (first author).

publications.name: CLaRE: CLIP with Latent Reconstruction Errors for Generated Face Detection
publications.publisher: Proceedings of the 1st ACM Workshop on Deepfake, Deception, and Disinformation Security
publications.summary: Research on deepfake detection using CLIP-based methods (co-author).

publications.name: On the Generalizability of 'Competition of Mechanisms: Tracing How Language Models Handle Facts and Counterfactuals'
publications.summary: A reproducibility study in LLM interpretability (first author).

work.name: Motive Engineering
work.summary: ML engineering and optimization work using C++, Python, PyTorch, CUDA, and Docker.

Created a combined DevOps/MLOps CD flow using Docker and pre-commits, reducing deliverable size tenfold and ensuring code reproducibility
Designed, implemented and optimized multiple object collision algorithms
Refactored legacy code to improve maintainability and use C++ 17 best practices
